_about: How every Open Asset Model asset type is made answerable, so coverage is a maintained invariant rather than a memory. A test (internal/lens, TestCoverageMapMatchesOAM) fails when OAM adds an asset type that is not classified here, when this file names a type OAM does not define, or when a lens entry names a lens that is neither a registered subject lens nor a declared legacy lens. surface is one of: lens (a dedicated curated lens, or lenses, report it); generic (collected and reachable only through the generic answer kinds — controlled, third_party, paths, table, hierarchy — with no dedicated lens yet); collection_pending (defined in OAM with annotated relations, but no collector populates it yet, so a lens would be empty); out_of_scope (intentionally unsupported for external attack surface). Every type, whatever its surface, is reachable through the schema-driven generic answer kinds (ai-design-principles.md, principle 1); this file records the curated surfacing on top of that. legacy_lenses are the lens commands served outside the subject-lens registry (internal/lens/cli). collected records whether a collector stores the type today. Update an entry when a lens or collector is added.

asset_types.note: The accounts lens computes platform accounts (code hosts, social media) from the subject's stored profile URLs, with the URL as evidence (principle 10); no collector stores Account assets yet. Observed-account collection (e.g. breach-exposure metadata keyed through the data-source system) is a separate planned collector.
Autonomous-system registration record; its name and holder are surfaced by the network and family lenses.
Surfaced by the network lens (announced prefixes, holder) and used by cloud/hosting attribution.
Registration and technical contacts; surfaced through the domains (registrant) and family (identity) lenses.
Registrar, expiry, transfer lock and DNSSEC are reported by the domains lens.
Defined in OAM (URL file, security.txt documents) but no collector stores File assets yet; reachable through generic traversal.
The most heavily covered type: names, resolution, services, certificates, DNS and web presence.
Financial transfers; outside the external attack surface Amass reports on. No lens planned.

LEI, tax, company and registry numbers and handles; reported by the identifiers lens, grouped by type, and used for corporate-group registration in org-group. Email identifiers also carry breach-exposure metadata recorded by the breach-exposure collector (XposedOrNot/HIBP, metadata only), surfaced by the identifiers lens.
Addresses, their hosting, cloud provider, services and geography.
Address-block registration record; surfaced by the network and geography lenses.
Stored places are reported by the geography lens.
Netblocks, who holds them, their cloud provider and hosting concentration.
Owners, corporate group, vendors, hosting, identity and duplicate resolution.
People tied to an organization or domain, and organizations recorded under a person's name.
Defined in OAM (contact phone numbers) but no collector stores Phone assets yet; reachable through generic traversal.
Software products on services, and their known vulnerabilities.
Software versions matched against vulnerability data; lifecycle is reported within the software checks.
Listening services, what they expose, their headers, software and web applications.
Certificates, their validity, authorities and the hosts they cover.
Websites, endpoints and off-domain URLs, with recognized web applications, reported by the web lens.
